sanskrit: śaraiḥ samantataḥ sarvaṃ khāṇḍavaṃ cāpi pāṇḍavaḥ chādayām āsa tad varṣam apakṛṣya tato vanāt
english: With arrows on every side the Pāṇḍava also covered all of Khāṇḍava, driving that rain-shower away from the forest.

sanskrit: na ca sma kiṃ cic chaknoti bhūtaṃ niścarituṃ tataḥ saṃchādyamāne khagamair asyatā savyasācinā
english: No creature whatsoever was able to escape from there, as the birds were covered by the shafts discharged by Savyasācin.

sanskrit: takṣakas tu na tatrāsīt sarparājo mahābalaḥ dahyamāne vane tasmin kurukṣetre 'bhavat tadā
english: But Takṣaka, the mighty king of serpents, was not there; while that forest burned, he was then at Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: aśvasenas tu tatrāsīt takṣakasya suto balī sa yatnam akarot tīvraṃ mokṣārthaṃ havyavāhanāt
english: But Ashvasena, Takṣaka's powerful son, was there; he strove intensely to free himself from the fire.

sanskrit: na śaśāka vinirgantuṃ kaunteyaśarapīḍitaḥ mokṣayām āsa taṃ mātā nigīrya bhujagātmajā
english: Pressed hard by the arrows of Kuntī's son, he could not escape; his mother, the serpent-born one, swallowed him and drew him free.

sanskrit: tasya pūrvaṃ śiro grastaṃ puccham asya nigīryate ūrdhvam ācakrame sā tu pannagī putragṛddhinī
english: His head was swallowed first, then his tail was being swallowed; the serpent-woman, eager for her son, moved swiftly upward.

sanskrit: tasyās tīkṣṇena bhallena pṛthudhāreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ śiraś ciccheda gacchantyās tām apaśyat sureśvaraḥ
english: With a sharp, broad-bladed arrow the Pāṇḍava severed her head as she was flying away; the lord of the gods saw her.

sanskrit: taṃ mumocayiṣur vajrī vātavarṣeṇa pāṇḍavam mohayām āsa tatkālam aśvasenas tv amucyata
english: The wielder of the thunderbolt, wishing to free him, bewildered the Pāṇḍava at that moment with a storm of wind and rain; and Ashvasena escaped.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca māyāṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā ghorāṃ nāgena vañcitaḥ dvidhā tridhā ca ciccheda khagatān eva bhārata
english: Seeing that dreadful illusion and having been tricked by the serpent, he cut the birds flying in the air into two and three pieces, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śaśāpa taṃ ca saṃkruddho bībhatsur jihmagāminam pāvako vāsudevaś ca apratiṣṭho bhaved iti
english: Bībhatsu in his fury cursed that crooked-moving one, and Pāvaka and Vāsudeva too, saying: "May he be without refuge."

sanskrit: tato jiṣṇuḥ sahasrākṣaṃ khaṃ vitatyeṣubhiḥ śitaiḥ yodhayām āsa saṃkruddho vañcanāṃ tām anusmaran
english: Then Jiṣṇu, enraged, filling the sky with sharp arrows, fought against the thousand-eyed one, remembering that deception.

sanskrit: devarāḍ api taṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃrabdham iva phalgunam svam astram asṛjad dīptaṃ yat tatānākhilaṃ nabhaḥ
english: The king of gods, seeing Phalguna inflamed with wrath, released his own blazing weapon, which spread across the entire sky.

sanskrit: tato vāyur mahāghoṣaḥ kṣobhayan sarvasāgarān viyatstho 'janayan meghāñ jaladhārāmuco ''kulān
english: Then a wind arose with a great roar, churning all the oceans, standing in the sky and producing clouds that poured forth torrents of water in tumult.

sanskrit: tadvighātārtham asṛjad arjuno 'py astram uttamam vāyavyam evābhimantrya pratipattiviśāradaḥ
english: To counter that, Arjuna too, expert in response, released the supreme wind-weapon, duly consecrated with its mantra.

sanskrit: tenendrāśanimeghānāṃ vīryaujas tadvināśitam jaladhārāś ca tāḥ śoṣaṃ jagmur neśuś ca vidyutaḥ
english: By that weapon the vigor and power of Indra's thunderbolt-clouds were destroyed; those torrents of water dried up, and the lightnings vanished.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena cābhavad vyoma saṃpraśāntarajastamaḥ sukhaśītānilaguṇaṃ prakṛtisthārkamaṇḍalam
english: In an instant the sky became calm, free of dust and darkness, characterized by a pleasant cool breeze, with the sun's orb restored to its natural state.

sanskrit: niṣpratīkārahṛṣṭaś ca hutabhug vividhākṛtiḥ prajajvālātulārciṣmān svanādaiḥ pūrayañ jagat
english: And the fire, which assumes many forms, rejoicing at having no more obstruction, blazed up with incomparable flames, filling the world with its roaring sounds.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇābhyāṃ rakṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca dāvam ahaṃkṛtāḥ samutpetur athākāśaṃ suparṇādyāḥ patatriṇaḥ
english: Seeing the forest fire protected by the two Kṛṣṇas, the Suparṇa birds and other winged creatures, filled with pride, rose up into the sky.

sanskrit: garuḍā vajrasadṛśaiḥ pakṣatuṇḍanakhais tathā prahartukāmāḥ saṃpetur ākāśāt kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: Garuḍas, with wings, beaks, and talons like thunderbolts, wishing to strike, swooped down from the sky upon Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tathaivoragasaṃghātāḥ pāṇḍavasya samīpataḥ utsṛjanto viṣaṃ ghoraṃ niścerur jvalitānanāḥ
english: Likewise masses of serpents, with flaming mouths, moved near the Pāṇḍava, pouring forth terrible venom.

sanskrit: tāṃś cakarta śaraiḥ pārthaḥ saroṣān dṛśya khecarān vivaśāś cāpatan dīptaṃ dehābhāvāya pāvakam
english: Pārtha cut down those infuriated sky-dwellers with his arrows as he saw them; helplessly they fell into the blazing fire for the dissolution of their bodies.

sanskrit: tataḥ surāḥ sagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ utpetur nādam atulam utsṛjanto raṇārthiṇaḥ
english: Then gods together with gandharvas, yakshas, rakshasas, and serpents rose up, releasing an incomparable roar, seeking battle.

sanskrit: ayaḥkaṇapacakrāśmabhuśuṇḍyudyatabāhavaḥ kṛṣṇapārthau jighāṃsantaḥ krodhasaṃmūrcchitaujasaḥ
english: With arms raised bearing iron pellets, discuses, stones, and muskets, their strength swooning with rage, they sought to kill Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha.

sanskrit: teṣām abhivyāharatāṃ śastravarṣaṃ ca muñcatām pramamāthottamāṅgāni bībhatsur niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: As they approached and released a rain of weapons, Bībhatsu smashed their heads with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaś ca sumahātejāś cakreṇārinihā tadā daityadānavasaṃghānāṃ cakāra kadanaṃ mahat
english: And Kṛṣṇa, of great brilliance, the slayer of foes, made great carnage among the hosts of Daityas and Dānavas with his discus.

sanskrit: athāpare śarair viddhāś cakravegeritās tadā velām iva samāsādya vyātiṣṭhanta mahaujasaḥ
english: Then others, pierced by arrows and driven by the force of the discus, the greatly powerful ones stood arrested as if having reached a shore.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakro 'bhisaṃkruddhas tridaśānāṃ maheśvaraḥ pāṇḍuraṃ gajam āsthāya tāv ubhau samabhidravat
english: Then Śakra, the great lord of the thirty gods, furiously enraged, mounting his white elephant, charged at both of them.

sanskrit: aśaniṃ gṛhya tarasā vajram astram avāsṛjat hatāv etāv iti prāha surān asurasūdanaḥ
english: Swiftly seizing the thunderbolt, the slayer of asuras released the weapon and said to the gods: "These two are slain."

sanskrit: tataḥ samudyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā devendreṇa mahāśanim jagṛhuḥ sarvaśastrāṇi svāni svāni surās tadā
english: Then seeing the great thunderbolt raised by the lord of gods, all the gods each took up their own weapons.

sanskrit: kāladaṇḍaṃ yamo rājā śibikāṃ ca dhaneśvaraḥ pāśaṃ ca varuṇas tatra vicakraṃ ca tathā śivaḥ
english: King Yama seized the staff of Death; the lord of wealth his litter; Varuṇa his noose; and Śiva too his discus.

sanskrit: oṣadhīr dīpyamānāś ca jagṛhāte 'śvināv api jagṛhe ca dhanur dhātā musalaṃ ca jayas tathā
english: The two Aśvins took up blazing medicinal herbs; Dhata seized his bow, and Jaya likewise his mace.

sanskrit: parvataṃ cāpi jagrāha kruddhas tvaṣṭā mahābalaḥ aṃśas tu śaktiṃ jagrāha mṛtyur devaḥ paraśvadham
english: The mighty Tvaṣṭā in his rage seized a mountain; Amshu seized a spear; and the god Mṛtyu seized an axe.

sanskrit: pragṛhya parighaṃ ghoraṃ vicacārāryamā api mitraś ca kṣuraparyantaṃ cakraṃ gṛhya vyatiṣṭhata
english: Taking up a terrible iron club, Aryaman too roamed about; and Mitra, taking up a discus edged with razors, stood ready.

sanskrit: pūṣā bhagaś ca saṃkruddhaḥ savitā ca viśāṃ pate āttakārmukanistriṃśāḥ kṛṣṇapārthāv abhidrutāḥ
english: Pusha, and Bhaga enraged, and Savitā, O lord of men, with bows and swords taken up, charged at Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha.

sanskrit: rudrāś ca vasavaś caiva marutaś ca mahābalāḥ viśvedevās tathā sādhyā dīpyamānāḥ svatejasā
english: The Rudras and the Vasus, and the mighty Maruts, the Viśvedevas and the Sādhyas likewise, blazed with their own radiance.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo devās tau puruṣottamau kṛṣṇapārthau jighāṃsantaḥ pratīyur vividhāyudhāḥ
english: These and many other gods, bearing various weapons, advanced against those two supreme beings, Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha, seeking to slay them.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutāny adṛśyanta nimittāni mahāhave yugāntasamarūpāṇi bhūtotsādāya bhārata
english: In that great battle, wondrous omens became visible, resembling those at the end of an age, for the destruction of beings, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tathā tu dṛṣṭvā saṃrabdhaṃ śakraṃ devaiḥ sahācyutau abhītau yudhi durdharṣau tasthatuḥ sajjakārmukau
english: Even so, seeing Śakra furious together with the gods, the two Achyutas stood fearless in battle, those invincible ones, with bows strung.

sanskrit: āgatāṃś caiva tān dṛṣṭvā devān ekaikaśas tataḥ nyavārayetāṃ saṃkruddhau bāṇair vajropamais tadā
english: And seeing those gods come, the two of them, enraged, repelled them one by one with arrows resembling thunderbolts.

sanskrit: asakṛd bhagnasaṃkalpāḥ surāś ca bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ bhayād raṇaṃ parityajya śakram evābhiśiśriyuḥ
english: The gods, their resolve broken again and again, were made to flee repeatedly; from fear they abandoned the battle and took refuge with Śakra alone.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā nivāritān devān mādhavenārjunena ca āścaryam agamaṃs tatra munayo divi viṣṭhitāḥ
english: Seeing the gods repelled by Mādhava and Arjuna, the sages stationed in heaven there were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: śakraś cāpi tayor vīryam upalabhyāsakṛd raṇe babhūva paramaprīto bhūyaś caitāv ayodhayat
english: And Śakra too, perceiving again and again their valor in battle, was supremely pleased, and yet again he fought against those two.

sanskrit: tato 'śmavarṣaṃ sumahad vyasṛjat pākaśāsanaḥ bhūya eva tadā vīryaṃ jijñāsuḥ savyasācinaḥ tac charair arjuno varṣaṃ pratijaghne 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ
english: Then the chastiser of Pāka released a tremendous shower of stones, wishing again to test the valor of Savyasācin; Arjuna, exceedingly wrathful, countered that shower with his arrows.

sanskrit: viphalaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ tat saṃprekṣya ca śatakratuḥ bhūyaḥ saṃvardhayām āsa tad varṣaṃ devarāḍ atha
english: Seeing that shower being made futile, the king of gods of a hundred sacrifices then greatly increased that shower again.

sanskrit: so 'śmavarṣaṃ mahāvegair iṣubhiḥ pākaśāsaniḥ vilayaṃ gamayām āsa harṣayan pitaraṃ tadā
english: The son of the chastiser of Pāka with swift arrows then caused that shower of stones to dissolve, bringing joy to his father.

sanskrit: samutpāṭya tu pāṇibhyāṃ mandarāc chikharaṃ mahat sadrumaṃ vyasṛjac chakro jighāṃsuḥ pāṇḍunandanam
english: Then Śakra, wishing to kill the son of Pāṇḍu, uprooted with his own hands a great peak from Mount Mandara, trees and all, and hurled it.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno vegavadbhir jvalitāgrair ajihmagaiḥ bāṇair vidhvaṃsayām āsa gireḥ śṛṅgaṃ sahasradhā
english: Then Arjuna, with swift, straight-flying arrows with blazing tips, shattered the mountain peak into a thousand pieces.

sanskrit: girer viśīryamāṇasya tasya rūpaṃ tadā babhau sārkacandragrahasyeva nabhasaḥ praviśīryataḥ
english: The appearance of that crumbling mountain then shone like the sky breaking apart together with sun, moon, and planets.

sanskrit: tenāvākpatatā dāve śailena mahatā bhṛśam bhūya eva hatās tatra prāṇinaḥ khāṇḍavālayāḥ
english: By that great mountain falling down into the fire, the creatures dwelling in Khāṇḍava were again greatly slain there.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā śailanipātena bhīṣitāḥ khāṇḍavālayāḥ dānavā rākṣasā nāgās tarakṣvṛkṣavanaukasaḥ dvipāḥ prabhinnāḥ śārdūlāḥ siṃhāḥ kesariṇas tathā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus terrified by the fall of the mountain, the inhabitants of Khāṇḍava — danavas, rakshasas, nagas, hyenas, tree-dwellers of the forest, elephants in rut, tigers, lions, and maned lions —

sanskrit: mṛgāś ca mahiṣāś caiva śataśaḥ pakṣiṇas tathā samudvignā visasṛpus tathānyā bhūtajātayaḥ
english: Deer and buffaloes, and birds by the hundreds, fled in agitation, and so too did other kinds of beings.

sanskrit: taṃ dāvaṃ samudīkṣantaḥ kṛṣṇau cābhyudyatāyudhau utpātanādaśabdena saṃtrāsita ivābhavan
english: Looking upon that conflagration and upon the two Kṛṣṇas with weapons raised, they seemed as if terrified by the sound of the crashing omens.

sanskrit: svatejobhāsvaraṃ cakram utsasarja janārdanaḥ tena tā jātayaḥ kṣudrāḥ sadānavaniśācarāḥ nikṛttāḥ śataśaḥ sarvā nipetur analaṃ kṣaṇāt
english: Janārdana released his discus blazing with its own radiance; with it all those petty creatures together with danavas and night-wanderers were cut down by the hundreds and in an instant fell into the fire.

sanskrit: adṛśyan rākṣasās tatra kṛṣṇacakravidāritāḥ vasārudhirasaṃpṛktāḥ saṃdhyāyām iva toyadāḥ
english: The rakshasas there, cloven by Kṛṣṇa's discus and mingled with fat and blood, were like rain-clouds at twilight.

sanskrit: piśācān pakṣiṇo nāgān paśūṃś cāpi sahasraśaḥ nighnaṃś carati vārṣṇeyaḥ kālavat tatra bhārata
english: The descendant of the Vṛṣṇis roamed there slaying pisachas, birds, nagas, and beasts by the thousands, like Death itself, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṣiptaṃ kṣiptaṃ hi tac cakraṃ kṛṣṇasyāmitraghātinaḥ hatvānekāni sattvāni pāṇim eti punaḥ punaḥ
english: That discus of Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of foes, thrown again and again, returned to his hand again and again after slaying many creatures.

sanskrit: tathā tu nighnatas tasya sarvasattvāni bhārata babhūva rūpam atyugraṃ sarvabhūtātmanas tadā
english: And as he slew all those creatures, O Bhārata, his form became exceedingly fierce — he who is the soul of all beings — at that time.

sanskrit: sametānāṃ ca devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ vijetā nābhavat kaś cit kṛṣṇapāṇḍavayor mṛdhe
english: Of all the assembled gods and danavas together, not one became a conqueror of Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava in battle.

sanskrit: tayor balāt paritrātuṃ taṃ dāvaṃ tu yadā surāḥ nāśaknuvañ śamayituṃ tadābhūvan parāṅmukhāḥ
english: When the gods were unable to rescue that forest from the power of those two, nor to extinguish it, then they turned away.

sanskrit: śatakratuś ca saṃprekṣya vimukhān devatāgaṇān babhūvāvasthitaḥ prītaḥ praśaṃsan kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: And Śatakratu, seeing the hosts of gods turned away, stood still, pleased, praising Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: nivṛtteṣu tu deveṣu vāg uvācāśarīriṇī śatakratum abhiprekṣya mahāgambhīraniḥsvanā
english: When the gods had withdrawn, a disembodied voice, deep and resonant, addressed Śatakratu, looking upon him.

sanskrit: na te sakhā saṃnihitas takṣakaḥ pannagottamaḥ dāhakāle khāṇḍavasya kurukṣetraṃ gato hy asau
english: "Your friend Takṣaka, best of serpents, is not present; at the time of Khāṇḍava's burning he has gone to Kurukṣetra."

sanskrit: na ca śakyau tvayā jetuṃ yuddhe 'smin samavasthitau vāsudevārjunau śakra nibodhedaṃ vaco mama
english: "Nor can these two who stand arrayed in this battle be conquered by you — Vāsudeva and Arjuna, O Śakra; hear this word of mine."

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇau devau tāv etau viśrutau divi bhavān apy abhijānāti yadvīryau yatparākramau
english: "These two are the gods Nara and Nārāyaṇa, renowned in heaven; you yourself know how great their valor and how great their prowess."

sanskrit: naitau śakyau durādharṣau vijetum ajitau yudhi api sarveṣu lokeṣu purāṇāv ṛṣisattamau
english: "These two, difficult to assail, unconquered in battle, cannot be vanquished; they are ancient and best among sages in all the worlds."

sanskrit: pūjanīyatamāv etāv api sarvaiḥ surāsuraiḥ sayakṣarakṣogandharvanarakiṃnarapannagaiḥ
english: "These two are most worthy of worship by all — gods and asuras together with yakshas, rakshasas, gandharvas, narakas, kinnaras, and serpents."

sanskrit: tasmād itaḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ gantum arhasi vāsava diṣṭaṃ cāpy anupaśyaitat khāṇḍavasya vināśanam
english: "Therefore, O Vāsava, you should depart from here together with the gods; regard also the destruction of Khāṇḍava as the decree of fate."

sanskrit: iti vācam abhiśrutya tathyam ity amareśvaraḥ kopāmarṣau samutsṛjya saṃpratasthe divaṃ tadā
english: Having heard that speech, the lord of immortals acknowledged it as true; relinquishing his anger and resentment, he then set out for heaven.

sanskrit: taṃ prasthitaṃ mahātmānaṃ samavekṣya divaukasaḥ tvaritāḥ sahitā rājann anujagmuḥ śatakratum
english: Seeing that great-souled one depart, the heavenly beings, O king, swiftly followed Śatakratu together.

sanskrit: devarājaṃ tadā yāntaṃ saha devair udīkṣya tu vāsudevārjunau vīrau siṃhanādaṃ vinedatuḥ
english: Seeing the king of gods then departing with the gods, the two heroes Vāsudeva and Arjuna roared with the roar of lions.

sanskrit: devarāje gate rājan prahṛṣṭau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau nirviśaṅkaṃ punar dāvaṃ dāhayām āsatus tadā
english: The king of gods having gone, O king, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava, overjoyed, then caused the forest fire to burn again without restraint.

sanskrit: sa māruta ivābhrāṇi nāśayitvārjunaḥ surān vyadhamac charasaṃpātaiḥ prāṇinaḥ khāṇḍavālayān
english: Like the wind destroying clouds, Arjuna, having driven off the gods, cut down with showers of arrows the living creatures dwelling in Khāṇḍava.

sanskrit: na ca sma kiṃ cic chaknoti bhūtaṃ niścarituṃ tataḥ saṃchidyamānam iṣubhir asyatā savyasācinā
english: No creature whatsoever was able to escape from there as it was cut apart by the arrows discharged by Savyasācin.

sanskrit: nāśakaṃs tatra bhūtāni mahānty api raṇe 'rjunam nirīkṣitum amogheṣuṃ kariṣyanti kuto raṇam
english: The creatures there, even the great ones, could not look upon Arjuna, whose shafts never miss, in battle — much less could they do battle.

sanskrit: śatenaikaṃ ca vivyādha śataṃ caikena patriṇā vyasavas te 'patann agnau sākṣāt kālahatā iva
english: With one arrow he pierced a hundred, and a hundred with a single shaft; lifeless they fell into the fire, as if struck down by Death himself.

sanskrit: na cālabhanta te śarma rodhaḥsu viṣameṣu ca pitṛdevanivāseṣu saṃtāpaś cāpy ajāyata
english: They found no shelter in embankments or in difficult terrain; even in the abodes of ancestors and gods distress arose.

sanskrit: bhūtasaṃghasahasrāś ca dīnāś cakrur mahāsvanam ruruvur vāraṇāś caiva tathaiva mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ tena śabdena vitresur gaṅgodadhicarā jhaṣāḥ
english: Thousands upon thousands of creatures in their misery raised a great cry; elephants bellowed, and so too deer and birds; at that sound the fish dwelling in the Gaṅgā and the ocean trembled.

sanskrit: na hy arjunaṃ mahābāhuṃ nāpi kṛṣṇaṃ mahābalam nirīkṣituṃ vai śaknoti kaś cid yoddhuṃ kutaḥ punaḥ
english: Indeed, no one was able even to look upon the mighty-armed Arjuna, nor upon the powerful Kṛṣṇa — much less to fight them.

sanskrit: ekāyanagatā ye 'pi niṣpatanty atra ke cana rākṣasān dānavān nāgāñ jaghne cakreṇa tān hariḥ
english: Those who fled even along a single path, whoever escaped there — rakshasas, danavas, and nagas — Hari slew them with his discus.

sanskrit: te vibhinnaśirodehāś cakravegād gatāsavaḥ petur āsye mahākāyā dīptasya vasuretasaḥ
english: Those great-bodied ones, their heads and bodies severed by the force of the discus, their lives gone, fell into the mouth of the blazing fire of golden seed.
